market_context: Thursday's AI and data-center selloff followed Democratic midterm wins. The Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 fell 4.4%. Friday is a partial rebound led by chips, and the strong October jobs report (+165K, unemployment 4.1%) lifted the odds of a December Fed hike to about 76-78%. The 10-year yield is 4.85%, the VIX is easing from its spike, and all three indexes are still headed for steep weekly losses.

predictions.reasoning: Dip-buying and a falling VIX (-13.7%) are supporting the rebound, and SPY is holding near the top of its day range after a historic one-day drop. Rate-hike fears and the 4.85% yield cap the upside, so I expect only a modest further gain into the close.

NVDA has already faded from its $194.90 high and now sits near the low of its range. It is still down 8% over five days, and the AI-regulation overhang and hike fears could keep capping the bounce. Chasing a one-day semiconductor rebound into a Friday close looks risky.
BTC is not taking part in the equity bounce, and the hot jobs report raised Fed hike odds to about 78%, which pressures risk assets. It is also trending lower, down 3.1% over five days.
